text:
Marathon Petroleum climbed 0.7% today to $400.59, extending a nearly 13% surge over two weeks as oil prices spiked on Middle East tensions. Brent crude topped $101 a barrel today—its highest since May—driven by escalating U.S.-Iran conflict and fears of supply disruptions. For a refiner like Marathon, higher crude prices can initially squeeze margins, but the company benefits when oil stays elevated because it locks in higher prices for the refined products (gasoline and diesel) it sells, and U.S. refineries are running at 98% capacity with relatively tight fuel inventories, limiting spare production to absorb price swings.

The broader geopolitical risk is supporting the entire energy complex right now. With President Trump publicly stating energy prices won't fall until after the midterm elections, markets are pricing in sustained elevated crude levels, which keeps refiners' margins healthy even as input costs rise.
